correctness.rationale: All distances checked: dist(a_i,b_i)=3 unique farthest; dist(a_i,b_j)=1 for j!=i, dist(a_i,a_j)=2. For same-part A-pair distance 2, a resolving other part has distances 1 and 3 (zero impossible), hence must be singleton {b_i} or {b_j}. Within A-occupancy r every pair forces one of its matched b singleton, so at least r-1 distinct B singletons; summing over q A-meeting parts yields n-q additional parts and lower n. Explicit n classes U0={a1,..,a_(n-1),b_n}, U1={a_n,b1}, singleton b2..b_(n-1) resolve each same-class pair; direct distance verification includes n=3. Independent exhaustive set-partition search finds minima n=3 and 4 with 122 and 2795 tested partitions. Thus all n are covered by combinatorial proof, not small enumeration.
residual_risks: Proof is metric-specific, not claimed for other matching-deletion or antipodal graphs.

value.rationale: The crown family is a standard 2-antipodal symmetric connected bipartite graph; exact strong partition dimension is a natural metric-location invariant. The n-valued classification closes the generic [2,n+1] gap and supplies an inductively reusable singleton-antipode charging obstruction, rather than a finite table, renaming or arbitrary instance.

final_claim: For every crown graph Cr_n=K_(n,n) with perfect matching removed and n>=3, the strong partition dimension pd_s(Cr_n)=n; any part with r A-side vertices forces at least r-1 matched singleton B-side parts.
limitations: No full enumeration/classification of minimum resolving partitions.
